A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Person2Drive benchmark and PDSA framework. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v2 includes supplementary material on pages 19–28; the supplied v3 ends after the references on page 18. This omission is a document difference, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: v2 reports original driving-data collection, closed-loop experiments, personalization results, indicator ablations and cross-scene analyses in its main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds alternative-formulation comparisons, a 50-participant preference study and a driver-specific behavior analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the DiffusionDrive base, BEV-conditioned 10-dimensional style model and trajectory-head fine-tuning using style-vector MSE. The missing supplementary implementation and post-processing descriptions do not establish that the underlying method changed.

E1.justification: The represented driving coverage remains Person2Drive, StyleDrive and Bench2Drive. Person2Drive's four routes were already documented in v2's supplement and are summarized in v3 Section 3.1. The new preference study evaluates existing routes without establishing a distinct driving task, environment or participant population; omitted cross-scene tables change the reported analyses rather than the documented dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Section 4.5 and Table 6 introduce an explicit comparison against direct style-vector supervision (DSV), behavior cloning (BC), inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) and preference learning (PL). This substantially broadens the evaluated comparison formulations beyond the retained baseline, DFT, PDSA-WB and ANC comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported validation designs change substantially: v3 adds preference testing with 50 participants on two routes and comparisons between personalized models under identical scenes. It omits v2's 6–14-indicator sweep and ten-driver, four-scene analysis. The eight/two route-repetition counts are relocated, not changed. Settings for the new alternative-formulation comparison are insufficiently specified to establish comparability with earlier scores.

E4.justification: v2's supplementary indicator-count sensitivity study and cross-scene behavioral and similarity analyses disappear, along with their supporting Tables 8–10. v3 instead adds human-preference validation and an analysis testing whether personalized policies capture driver-specific behavior under fixed scenes. These substantially change the supporting analyses, while the main BEV ablations and trajectory examples remain.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same per-driver mean/variance reporting, fractions of drivers improving and Wilcoxon signed-rank statement with p<0.001. No changed seed, repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure is stated. Omitted supplementary Table 10 removes results using the existing mean/variance convention rather than introducing a different reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports MMDSS values of 0.6690/0.6811/0.6591/0.6796/0.7055 for DSV/BC/IRL/PL/PDSA. Table 7 adds PDSA preference rates of 76% and 72%, versus 24% and 28% for baseline; Section 4.5 adds inter-driver similarities of 0.6383 and 0.6716. Supplementary indicator-count and cross-scene results disappear. Retained main-table values are unchanged, including PDSA's 0.6800 average; the new 0.7055 is not established as a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The supplementary definition MMDdiff = MMDintra − MMDinter in v2 Equation (4) disappears with its indicator-count analysis. The main mathematical definitions in Equations (1)–(3) remain unchanged, and no new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: personalized driving-data collection, quantitative style evaluation and lightweight style-guided adaptation while preserving driving performance. The added validation supports these existing claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 omits substantive limitations concerning weak base-model driving competence, safety interventions suppressing style expression and validation using only DiffusionDrive. It adds interpretations linking preference results to human perception and fixed-scene comparisons to driver specificity. Section 5.2 also narrows its interpretation from not compromising safety to not degrading driving performance.

D1.justification: The omitted supplement contained sensor specifications, collection hardware and fixed-weather conditions, participant demographics, trajectory encoding and dropout, 20-proposal alignment details, waypoint sampling, PID parameters and TTC/distance-based braking overrides. Only selected dataset totals and repetition counts move into Section 3.1. v3 also removes the abstract's commitment to release code and data after acceptance without providing replacement access information.

R1.justification: The same 34 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. The added E2E-AD qualifier in Section 3.2 clarifies the scope already established elsewhere; it does not materially reposition the contribution against prior research.

P1.justification: The document loses its entire supplementary structure covering dataset details, implementation, further experiments and limitations. Selected dataset information moves into Section 3.1, while Section 4.5 and acknowledgements are added. Most retained main-text prose remains unchanged apart from localized edits. References to supplementary material persist despite its absence from v3.

P2.justification: v3 omits supplementary Figures 7–9 and Tables 7–10, adds two validation tables, and transposes the ANC comparison in Table 5. The retained safety table becomes Table 8, and several figures are relocated through reflow. Figure 1 receives a label refinement. This substantially changes the evidence display beyond simple renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Section 4.5 adds useful comparison and human-preference evidence, but v3 loses the detailed inference controls and limitations needed to reproduce and interpret its retained personalization and safety claims. The omitted supplement explicitly disclosed safety overrides, their suppression of style expression and reliance on one base model; it also supplied indicator-selection and cross-scene evidence. Losing these substantially weakens reproducibility and transparency. The briefly specified new validation does not compensate for those material losses.
